cities.name: Asheville
cities.subtitle: Downtown public art, native gardens and family science
intro: Asheville can be explored without treating the mountains and downtown as a single hurried itinerary. Start at the city's central public square, then choose a separate nature outing near the university or an indoor science visit.

Pack Square Park is a useful downtown starting point, while Asheville Botanical Garden focuses on Southern Appalachian plants and limits certain activities to protect them. The interactive Asheville Museum of Science provides a ticketed option when a family wants indoor learning.
cities.before: Check park events, garden access, storms and current museum hours before heading out. The Botanical Garden explicitly prohibits pets other than service dogs.

places.name: Pack Square Park
places.desc: This downtown green space brings walking paths, public art and a popular seasonal splashpad into one central area. It's a relaxed family stop, although live programming and splashpad operation need a check before visiting.
places.note: General public park access is free; check special-event fees and splashpad schedules.
places.petNote: City park dogs must stay on leash; follow local restrictions.

places.name: Asheville Botanical Garden
places.desc: Explore the region's native plants on paths designed for quiet nature study rather than sports. Families are welcome with supervision, but the operator forbids pets except service dogs.
places.note: Admission and parking are free. Some paths are not accessible to all visitors; no dogs or other pets except service animals.

places.name: Asheville Museum of Science (AMOS)
places.desc: This downtown museum gives children and adults hands-on ways to explore science and the environment. General admission is paid for most visitors, with some age-based and eligibility discounts listed by the museum.
places.note: Check the official ticket page for current prices, available exhibits and operating hours. No dedicated on-site parking.

cities.name: Indianapolis

cover.file: Indianapolis from White River State Park.jpg
cover.author: Julie

cities.subtitle: Waterside walks, hands-on exhibits and a landmark library
intro: Indianapolis combines a downtown public park with cultural sites that work on quite different schedules. A White River State Park stroll offers a low-cost starting point before choosing which ticketed activities merit more time.

The Children's Museum of Indianapolis is an interactive family attraction north of downtown; Central Library offers a free indoor alternative. Plan these as separate stops and check live driving or transit distances rather than assuming all three are adjacent.
cities.before: Museum admission prices depend on the selected day; parking and rentals can have additional costs. Use the official visitor pages to verify schedules and any temporary exhibit closures.

places.name: White River State Park
places.desc: The canal and surrounding downtown green spaces offer an easy walking outing without buying a museum ticket. Families can explore the paths, while neighboring attractions and boat rentals are separate paid choices.
places.note: Free park entry, but parking, rentals and attractions may charge. Park rules permit leashed dogs on leashes no longer than six feet.

photo.file: Indianapolis from White River State Park.jpg
photo.author: Julie

places.petNote: Dogs on leashes up to six feet are allowed under park rules.

places.name: The Children's Museum of Indianapolis
places.price: Paid admission — prices vary by date
places.desc: Hands-on exhibits connect science, history and creativity for families and younger visitors. Prices vary depending on your visit date, so select tickets on the official site before planning a full museum day.
places.note: Advance reservations are recommended; verify date-specific rates and closures. Most visits require paid admission.

places.name: Indianapolis Central Library
places.address: 40 E St. Clair St., Indianapolis, IN 46204
places.desc: The Central Library brings a historic limestone structure together with a modern glass-and-steel addition. It offers a quiet indoor setting for books and architecture without a general admission ticket.
places.note: Entry to the public library is free. Check the official branch page for opening hours, events and individual room restrictions.

cities.name: Portland
cities.subtitle: Free rose gardens, interactive science and a city-block bookstore
intro: Portland's attractions reward planning by neighborhood rather than packing every destination into one walking route. The International Rose Test Garden occupies a hillside garden setting, while OMSI is across the river in a separate district.

Powell's City of Books adds an independent indoor stop where browsing is free but shopping is optional. Consider separating the rose garden, museum and bookstore into different parts of a day, and check transit or map directions for current travel time.
cities.before: Rose blooms change by season; the rose garden has limited paid parking. Check OMSI's updated exhibitions and ticket details, and verify the bookstore's opening schedule with its official site.

places.name: International Rose Test Garden
places.desc: A large rose garden in Washington Park gives visitors free outdoor paths, planting displays and views of the city. Parking can cost extra and the City of Portland explicitly requires dogs to stay on leash.
places.note: Free public garden admission. Parking can cost extra and access may change for events or maintenance.
places.petNote: The City of Portland states all dogs must be leashed in this park.

places.name: Oregon Museum of Science and Industry (OMSI)
places.desc: OMSI's interactive science spaces are designed for hands-on discovery across several age groups. General entry is paid, and selected exhibitions, presentations or experiences can require additional tickets.
places.note: Check the museum's current admission calendar, closures and optional ticket upgrades on its official website.

photo.author: Gary Halvorson / Oregon State Archives

places.name: Powell's City of Books
places.price: Free to browse; purchases cost extra
places.desc: The famous independent bookstore provides a city-block collection of books to browse at your own pace. Entry does not require a ticket, but shopping and optional purchases are separate costs.
places.note: Browsing has no admission fee. Check current shop hours and any special-event rules on the retailer's official site.

notes: Original, officially sourced editorial records for second batch of city guides; verify changing details before each trip.
